messages:
aj: quick one — our canary healthcheck started getting 401s after I switched to mounting the api key from a k8s secret. curl inside the pod fails, but same header works from my laptop. anyone seen this?

maria: usually newline/whitespace when secrets are mounted. are you using `echo` to create the secret?

aj: yeah, created via: `kubectl create secret generic app-key --from-literal=API_KEY=abc123...` then in the pod we do `Authorization: Basic <base64>` where base64 is base64(username+":"+API_KEY). curl locally: `-H "Authorization: Basic <same>"` -> 200. In pod -> 401.

samir: check for trailing \n. If the secret has a newline the base64 changes. inside pod do: `cat /etc/secret/API_KEY | od -c` to see hidden chars.

emily: also double-check whatever code builds the header — some SDKs will urlsafe/base64 or auto-prepend credentials if you pass them as a separate param. which client are you using?

aj: it's a small Go service using net/http with `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+b64)` — I generate b64 locally with `echo -n 'service:'$API_KEY | base64`. In the pod I printed the env var with `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | base64` and it matched what I used locally, but request still 401.

maria: are you certain the pod process is reading env var and not the file path? we mount secret as file and also inject env var from file in the deployment: `valueFrom: secretKeyRef`. K8s sometimes preserves trailing newline depending on how secret was created.

samir: another gotcha — some HTTP proxies strip or alter Authorization header. are you hitting an ingress or sidecar (envoy) in cluster? ingress might be doing `auth` or rewriting. Try curling the upstream from the pod (bypass ingress) to see if source of 401 is before or after proxy.

aj: good call — it's behind our internal envoy. I did a direct curl to service IP and got 200. with envoy -> 401.

emily: envoy config might be removing authorization for HTTP/2 upgrade or if multiple `Authorization` headers exist. check envoy access logs. Also verify canonicalization: Basic header must be exactly `Basic <base64>` with single space and no trailing CRLF inside the token.

maria: side note on creating secrets portably: when scripting use `printf` not `echo` so no newline: `printf '%s' "${API_KEY}" | base64 -w0` (linux) or `printf '%s' "${API_KEY}" | base64` (mac). For scripting in CI, `echo -n` is ok but inconsistent across shells.

aj: thanks — discovered the token file accidentally had a CRLF from a windows editor when the secret was added by a teammate. fixed with `tr -d '\r'` before creating secret and envoy stopped dropping the header.

emily: nice. bookmarking this: common checklist for basic-auth debug in infra: 1) verify env/file contents (od/xxd), 2) confirm base64 equals expected, 3) curl upstream vs via proxy, 4) inspect proxy logs, 5) watch for SDK/client auto-auth behavior.

infra-bot: deploy 18565.2 -> canary rolled back automatically (401s) :warning: — rollback reason: upstream auth failures.

samir: oh and tiny tip for other langs: Python requests `requests.auth.HTTPBasicAuth(user, pw)` will set header for you; if you craft header manually, make sure to `encode('utf-8')` before base64. In node: `Buffer.from(user+":"+key, 'utf8').toString('base64')`.

maria: and for kubernetes manifests: when referencing file->env use `envFrom` or `valueFrom` consistently; prefer `--from-file` when adding secrets that are binary tokens so you don't accidentally get newline transformations.

aj: all good now. thanks everyone :clap:. saved a snippet to the runbook.

emily: could you drop the minimal repro (how the secret was created + envoy log line) into #incidents or the runbook doc? helps others.

aj: will do.
